title: Apply laboratory quality standards and legislative requirements to ensure accurate, reproducible and reliable seed testing quality outputs and traceability

lessons.title: Applying quality controls in daily laboratory work
lessons.html:
Quality is built into each step

In this practical module you apply the laboratory's quality management system in real work. The aim is that any result issued can be reproduced, defended and traced back to the sample, the analyst, the equipment and the method.

Sample receipt and traceability

  • Register every sample with a unique laboratory number on arrival.
  • Record date, client, species, cultivar, lot number, tests requested and condition of seals.
  • Label all working samples and test units (germination rolls, trays, moisture tins) with the laboratory number.
  • Store submitted and retained samples under controlled conditions for the required retention period.

Equipment control

EquipmentControl
BalancesExternal calibration; daily check with reference masses before use
Ovens and germinatorsTemperature mapping; continuous logging; alarm limits
DividersCheck for damage and correct operation; clean between samples
Thermometers and data loggersCalibration traceable to national standards
Moisture metersCalibration against the oven reference method

Do not use equipment that is overdue for calibration or has failed a check. Label it out of service and report it.

Method control

Use the current edition of the ISTA Rules and the laboratory's controlled procedures. Record any deviation, its reason and its approval, and state it on the report where required.

Analyst competence

Only authorised analysts perform and sign off each test. Keep training records, and take part in internal comparisons and ISTA proficiency tests. Discuss any proficiency result outside the acceptable range and take corrective action.

Internal quality checks

  • Replicate tolerance checks on every germination and purity test.
  • Repeat testing of retained samples by a different analyst.
  • Control samples of known quality run alongside routine samples.

lessons.title: Records, non-conformities and legal compliance
lessons.html:
Records that stand up to scrutiny

Raw data are the proof behind every result. Accreditation assessors, regulators and clients may ask to see them.

  • Record observations at the time they are made, in ink or in the validated electronic system.
  • Never erase or overwrite; correct by striking through so the original remains legible, then initial and date.
  • Record who did each step and which equipment was used.
  • Keep records for the period required by law, the accreditation body and the client.

Reporting results

  1. Check calculations and tolerance compliance.
  2. Have results technically reviewed by an authorised person.
  3. Issue on the correct report or certificate format with sample and lot identification, methods, results and any deviations.
  4. Never issue an ISTA certificate unless the laboratory is accredited for that test and the rules for that certificate were followed.

Handling non-conformities

A non-conformity is any departure from requirements: a germinator temperature excursion, an expired reagent used, a mislabelled sample, a proficiency test failure.

  1. Stop the affected work and contain the problem.
  2. Assess impact on results already issued; recall or amend reports if needed and inform clients.
  3. Find the root cause.
  4. Implement corrective action and check its effectiveness.
  5. Record everything in the non-conformity register.

Legislative compliance

Results are used to show compliance with the minimum standards and labelling requirements under the Plant Improvement Act 53 of 1976 and its regulations, and with certification scheme rules. Confirm with your organisation which version of seed legislation and regulations is currently in force. For export, phytosanitary and importing-country requirements may also apply. Keep a legal register, and apply rule changes from their effective dates.

Impartiality

Report results as found. Pressure to change a result for commercial reasons must be refused and reported to the quality manager.

Audits

Take part in internal audits and external assessments openly. Audits are a tool to improve the system, not a threat.

Key points

  • Give every sample a unique number and label every test unit with it.
  • Use only calibrated, checked equipment; take faulty items out of service.
  • Record raw data at the time, and correct without erasing.
  • Contain, assess, fix the root cause and record every non-conformity.
  • Report results impartially in line with legislation and accreditation rules.
